title: Full research pass review of the coptic lane, 2026-10-19
semantics: Project-created review metadata. Versions include witnesses, components, translations and unresolved leads; their count is not a count of substantive revisions. Acquisition does not establish transcription, collation, normative revision or local reception. No ancestry is asserted.

review_files.storage: untracked workspace scratch; pinned here by SHA-256 only

uses.label: Coptic Catholic Church (Patriarchate of Alexandria of the Copts)
uses.finding: The Church's own retrospective book list (1736–2009, 68 numbered entries, one number skipped) identifies the 1736 Tuki three-anaphora book, the Cairo 1898 Euchologion, the Rome 1971 Euchologion, deacon's books of 1875 and 1898, Cairo lectionaries from 1900 onward and a series of separately printed Basil liturgies from 1952 to 2009. A church-hosted comparison article reports a postconciliar revision of the Basil text: a proposal in April 1975, a synodal commission in May 1976, a provisional text circulated for comment and a final text issued on 25 February 1990 under Patriarch Stephanos II, with before/after prayer texts. The public manuscript catalogue of the Bohairic Coptic Euchologia Project identifies two manuscript Euchologia as Coptic Catholic by their contents (Coptic Museum Liturgy 265 and BnF Arabe 5969), one of them with a later correction layer. A full-view public-domain copy of the 1898 Euchologion is catalogued at HathiTrust but could not be retrieved.
uses.limit: No original 1898, 1934, 1971, 1987 or 1990 book was acquired or inspected; the 1990 revision rests on a church-hosted 2013 article quoting the patriarchal preface. The church list disclaims completeness and stops in 2009. Catholic attribution of the two manuscripts rests on a 2026 autoptic catalogue entry, not on images inspected in this pass.
next_sources: HathiTrust oxu1.308011427 (1898 Euchologion, full view) through an interactive or institutional route
Original 1971 Rome Euchologion and the 1990 Basil liturgy with its patriarchal preface (Coptic Catholic Patriarchate, Cairo; Pontifical Oriental Institute library)
Synodus Alexandrina Coptorum 1898 (Rome 1899), HathiTrust record 103390316, for liturgical decrees bearing on the 1898 books
Gallica images of BnF Arabe 5969 and Coptic Museum images of Liturgy 265
uses.review_remaining_gap: No Coptic Catholic printed book after 1736 inspected in the original; 1898 full view at HathiTrust refused (HTTP 403, also on this reviewer's single probe); 1934 Catholic book unlocated beyond Hammerschmidt; 1971, 1987–2009 and 1990 books unseen; provisional 1976–1990 text unidentified; list ends 2009 and disclaims completeness.

uses.label: Bohairic Coptic manuscript tradition (shared ancestry and collateral witnesses)
uses.finding: Vat. copt. 17 (dated 1288) is now held as the complete offered image sequence. The BCEP autoptic record describes its contents (Basil, Gregory and Cyril with pre-anaphora and occasional prayers), its production at the Monastery of St Antony, a later binding bearing Roman Catholic arms with the Latin spine title 'Liturgia Copta', and a Latin marginal direction at the institution narrative in Gregory (ff. 81r–v). Image 0082 (ff. 80v–81r) was viewed and shows that Latin marginal note beside the bread words. The 2026 manuscript surveys describe a repertoire of roughly 320 to 375 Bohairic Euchologia with variable celebrant prayers.
uses.limit: A Latin marginal note and a later binding show Western readers or owners, not Catholic liturgical reception. No manuscript is shown to be Tuki's exemplar. The manuscript repertoire is labelled as a lead, not as recensions.
next_sources: Full BCEP catalogue observations and manuscript images for the Asyut-associated family and Catholic-period manuscripts
Chaîne 1912 p. 228 n. 2 versus Vat. copt. 17 and Vat. copt. 18 contents for Tuki's exemplar
uses.review_remaining_gap: Observations of 317 BCEP documents not read individually by the researcher; no images of the Paris, Huntington or Cairo anchors; Tuki's exemplar open (Vat. copt. 18 and BnF Copt. 26 with Ascari's 1736 note are leads).

uses.label: Southern Egyptian (Sahidic) Eucharistic use of the White Monastery, extinct
uses.finding: Four fragmentary Sahidic Euchologia (MONB.VD, MONB.VE, MONB.VF and MONB.VG) are presented by the Göttingen Sahidic Euchologia project with images and diplomatic transcriptions; all publicly offered images and all transcriptions were acquired. MONB.VE is Lanne's Great Euchologion, which preserves fragments of thirteen anaphoras and is dated to the end of the tenth century through a scribal hand matched to a colophon of 990. The project places the four codices before the reform of Patriarch Gabriel II ibn Turaik (1131–1145), which it says reduced the formularies to Basil, Gregory and Cyril.
uses.limit: Fragmentary manuscripts; dates are palaeographic and the sources disagree for MONB.VF and MONB.VG. No lineal relationship to any Catholic book is asserted. 87 page slots were provider placeholders (not extant or protected).
uses.review_remaining_gap: Fragmentary codices; 87 placeholder slots; no relation to Catholic books asserted; Lanne 1958 and Suciu 2011 not acquired.

uses.label: Coptic Orthodox printed Euchologia (collateral, not Catholic)
uses.finding: The Cairo 1902 Euchologion of 'Abd al-Masih Salib al-Mas'udi is now held whole (793-page Bonn PDF); its title page calls it the first edition, printed at the 'Ayn Shams press in 1618 of the Martyrs (1902). Kammerer and Hammerschmidt list further Orthodox editions of 1887, 1921, 1924, 1926, 1927, 1932, 1934 and 1936; Störk (reported by the reviewer) adds 1960 and 1984 and doubts a separate 1904 Labib edition.
uses.limit: These books are comparison controls only. A shared title or a shared Cairo press does not establish Catholic use.
uses.review_remaining_gap: 1887 books, 1921–1936 editions, 1960 and 1984 uninspected; Labib 1904 existence unresolved; Störk p. 30 only as indexed text.

uses.label: Greek-language Egyptian Euchologia in the Coptic manuscript tradition
uses.finding: The reviewer's BCEP export lists Greek-in-Coptic-script and Greek–Arabic Euchologia (for example BnF Grec 325 and Kacmarcik MS 6, both fourteenth century by palaeography). Early Greek Mark witnesses are already in the inventory.
uses.limit: Not examined in this pass; Greek language does not imply Byzantine ecclesial use.
next_sources: BCEP records 608279 and 608321 and their image routes
uses.review_remaining_gap: All images and observations of the Greek-language Egyptian euchologia.
